topic: What power allocation trade-offs arise from differing scan losses between quasi-TEM and quasi-TE1 modes for multi-beam satellite systems?
consensus_response: Differing scan losses between quasi-TEM and quasi-TE1 modes significantly impact power allocation in multi-beam satellite systems. Quasi-TEM modes offer lower scan losses, optimizing power usage for higher throughput but increasing interference. Conversely, quasi-TE1 modes have higher scan losses, reducing overall system capacity but decreasing interference. Mode-Adaptive Power Allocation (MAPA) and Joint Resource Allocation and Power Control (JRAPC) can be integrated to dynamically adjust power allocation based on real-time changes in traffic demands, scan losses, and interference levels. This approach optimizes resource utilization while maintaining fairness among users and minimizing delay constraints.
